rules.statement: Route every server-initiated outbound HTTP call to a client-controlled URL (fetches and POST deliveries alike) through a dedicated named HttpClient whose handler uses the shared SSRF guard as its ConnectCallback and sets AllowAutoRedirect = false; never use the default unnamed HttpClient for such calls.
rules.why: The default client follows redirects and applies no SSRF control, so a client registering an internal URL can turn the server into a confused deputy that probes internal services or follows a redirect to an internal host.
rules.check: Look for outbound calls to client-registered URLs (e.g. logout or notification endpoints, metadata URIs) made with IHttpClientFactory.CreateClient() with no name, or with a named client whose handler lacks the guard ConnectCallback or leaves auto-redirect enabled.

rules.statement: Read an outbound HTTP response body from a client-controlled URL through the shared capped reader, which rejects early on Content-Length and still enforces the byte cap while streaming; never call ReadAsStringAsync/ReadAsByteArrayAsync on it with no cap.
rules.why: An uncapped read lets an oversized response exhaust resources (DoS), and Content-Length can be missing or false, so it is only a hint.
rules.check: Look for ReadAsStringAsync, ReadAsByteArrayAsync or an unbounded stream copy on responses fetched from client-supplied URLs, or for a copied capped-read helper instead of the shared one.

rules.statement: A fetch of a client-supplied URL that reads the response body must require an absolute https URI, apply the optional host allow-list, and bound the request with a timeout CancellationTokenSource linked to the caller's token.
rules.why: These checks give every client-URL fetch the same SSRF and resource bounds, so no fetch path is left weaker than the others.
rules.check: New or changed client-URL fetches that accept non-https or relative URIs, skip the allow-list check, or have no linked timeout token.

rules.statement: When a timeout is enforced with a linked CancellationTokenSource, turn only the timeout's cancellation into a domain error and let the caller's own cancellation propagate unchanged.
rules.why: Real caller cancellation must not be masked as a fetch failure.
rules.check: catch (OperationCanceledException) blocks that turn every cancellation into an error without checking whether the caller's token requested it.

rules.statement: Surface specific validation failures (wrong status code, content type, or size) as their own errors instead of wrapping them in a generic 'failed to fetch' error.
rules.why: Masking the specific failure hides the real cause from callers and from diagnostics.
rules.check: Broad catch blocks around a fetch-and-validate sequence that replace a specific validation error with a generic one.

rules.statement: Stream-reading helpers should write into a caller-supplied IBufferWriter<byte> (a pooled NCode.Buffers writer) and the caller should parse directly from the resulting ReadOnlySequence<byte>, rather than the helper allocating and returning a byte[].
rules.why: This avoids an intermediate array allocation, allows zero-copy JsonDocument.Parse, and returns the buffers to the pool.
rules.check: Helpers that return byte[] or string from a body read, or callers that call ToArray() on the buffer before parsing when a sequence-based parse is available.

rules.statement: Do not add settings or options for a behavior that has no real need for them (for example, body size or timeout settings on a call whose response body is thrown away).
rules.why: Settings that serve no purpose add speculative public surface.
rules.check: New public options or settings properties on code paths where they control nothing that matters.

rules.statement: Extract logic that is duplicated across consumers into one shared service instead of copying it, and register that service with TryAddSingleton so hosts can override it through DI.
rules.why: Duplicated copies drift apart, and TryAdd registration keeps the shared seam replaceable.
rules.check: The same helper method copied into several classes, or a shared service registered with AddSingleton instead of TryAddSingleton.
